text: A REST step is a flow action, dropped into the canvas just like any trigger or action you've already used in this course. Configuring one really means filling in five real fields: the HTTP method, the endpoint URL, the headers, the request body, and how the response gets mapped back. Method is GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, or DELETE, matching whatever the external API expects.

The endpoint URL usually isn't typed in as a raw string sitting inside one flow. In a well-built flow it's built from a Connection and Credential Alias instead — a reusable record that stores the base URL and the authentication profile once, centrally and securely. Rotate the credential in one place, and every flow referencing that alias automatically picks up the change, instead of someone having to hunt down every flow that hardcoded it.

Everything you already know about data pills applies directly here. Going in, the request body is usually built from data pills carried forward from the trigger or earlier actions — an incident's number, or its short description, inserted straight into the JSON payload sent to the external system. Coming out, the REST step's response mapping lets you pull a specific field out of the JSON that comes back and turn it into a brand new data pill, exactly like any other action's output.

That new data pill behaves like any other output in the flow — a notification step, a record update, even another REST step further down the canvas can reference it the same way it references anything else. The REST step itself sits between the tools you already know: more structured than a Script step, since there's no code at all, and more general than a spoke, since it isn't limited to systems that happen to have a pre-built action set.
Reach for a spoke first when one exists for the system you're integrating with, and reach for the REST step when it doesn't. Next up: a worked scenario that combines both inside a single flow.
